title: Ask about one link in a chain
statement: A cause question over a chain of causes must name the one link it asks about, because 'what causes this?' makes several links defensible.
example: Six practice items were dropped after a quality screen showed more than one defensible key, traced to causal-chain passages asked 'what causes X?'.
detail: A cross-family quality screen of Grade 3 items that had passed a blind-solve gate showed six practice items with more than one defensible key, each confirmed by reading it; the report gives the root cause as a passage built as a causal chain with a 'what causes X?' prompt, made worse when the key is set on a link further back to defeat blind solvers. A QA pass over a shared item bundle confirmed a matching item with several correct answers for the same reason, and the report calls for a single-link redesign of chain-based items.

evidence.quote: 6 practice items dropped after the screen credibly showed a **multi-defensible key**
Root cause: a causal-**chain** passage + a "what causes X?" prompt makes several links defensible, and anti-leak keying the *non-proximate* link worsens it.
The passage is one continuous transitive causal chain
chain-based hot-text/EBSR need a single-link redesign (a future round)
